LESSON: PILLARS OF ISLAM

Grade: PP1
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: DEVOTIONAL
Topic 3.1: Pillars of Islam

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Pillars of Islam. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: what they have heard 2. Who says the shahadah?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Pillars of Islam means in simple pupil language
2. give 3 correct examples of Pillars of Islam from Kenya
3. practise Pillars of Islam in clear steps
4. apply Pillars of Islam in one real-life situation this week

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: PILLARS OF ISLAM
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: PP1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Pillars of Islam helps you succeed in ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: PILLARS OF ISLAM
Study Pillars of Islam like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain what Pillars of Islam means in simple pupil language

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Pillars of Islam means in simple pupil language. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Pillars of Islam means in simple pupil language.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Pillars of Islam” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Pillars of Islam means in simple pupil language. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give 3 correct examples of Pillars of Islam from Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to give 3 correct examples of Pillars of Islam from Kenya. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give 3 correct examples of Pillars of Islam from Kenya.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Pillars of Islam in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give 3 correct examples of Pillars of Islam from Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise Pillars of Islam in clear steps

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Pillars of Islam in clear steps. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Pillars of Islam in clear steps.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Pillars of Islam in clear steps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply Pillars of Islam in one real-life situation this week

What this means
In this part you learn to apply Pillars of Islam in one real-life situation this week. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply Pillars of Islam in one real-life situation this week.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Pillars of Islam” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply Pillars of Islam in one real-life situation this week. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Pillars of Islam is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Pillars of Islam” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: explain what Pillars of Islam means in simple pupil language)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Pillars of Islam in your own words. (skill: give 3 correct examples of Pillars of Islam from Kenya)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: practise Pillars of Islam in clear steps)

Example 4: Show how “Pillars of Islam” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: apply Pillars of Islam in one real-life situation this week)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Pillars of Islam to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Pillars of Islam means in simple pupil language.
3. Practise this skill: give 3 correct examples of Pillars of Islam from Kenya.
4. Practise this skill: practise Pillars of Islam in clear steps.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Pillars of Islam from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Pillars of Islam: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study Pillars of Islam?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. what they have heard 2. Who says the shahadah?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Pillars of Islam means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Pillars of Islam means in simple pupil language.
5. Be able to: give 3 correct examples of Pillars of Islam from Kenya.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
